amendments.rule: Be displaced by a possessive: `τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ` → *of his will*. The article is `unrepresented`, the possessive belongs to `αὐτοῦ`, and *of* stays with the noun. Displacement is what a genitive pronoun does, so where there is no such pronoun the article is not displaced and is not `unrepresented`: it is what the supplied possessive realizes. `ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ` → *in my heart*, `τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν` → *our redemption*, `τὸν ἄνδρα` → *her husband* align the article to *my*, *our*, *her*, headed there, with any case preposition riding along as in rule 21. Do not mark such a possessive `added`: rule 11 makes the ASV's italics evidence, not a verdict. The test is whether some other word is present to take the possessive; if one is, rule 20 proper applies and the article realizes no determiner. A genitive pronoun is the ordinary case, but not the only one: a possessive dative does it (`εἰς τὴν χρείαν μοι` → *unto my need*, with *my* on `μοι`), a genitive demonstrative does it (`τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ` → *by their disobedience*, with *their* on `τούτων`), and so does a genitive noun or name the ASV renders with *'s* (`τῆς Καίσαρος οἰκίας` → *Caesar's household*, `ὁ θρόνος τοῦ Σατανᾶ` → *Satan's throne*). What matters is that the English possessive already has a source word to belong to, not the case that word is in. What displacement empties is the **determiner slot** and nothing else, so an article whose determiner another word has taken is not thereby emptied of an English word of some other kind the ASV supplies for it. Where the ASV writes such an article a separate **antecedent pronoun** under rule 92, or an **address word** under rule 89, the article takes that word and the possessive still belongs to the possessor: `μου τὴν σάρκα` → *them that are my flesh* gives *my* to `μου`, *them* to the article, and the discontinuous *that are … flesh* to `σάρκα` under rule 15, exactly as rule 89's REV.19.5 gives *ye* to an article whose possessive slot `αὐτοῦ` already occupies. An antecedent pronoun is not a determiner, and a possessor cannot displace what is not one. The contrast is an antecedent some other source token already spells: where the Greek expresses the word the relative clause is predicated of, the article has nothing left to take and is `unrepresented` under rule 23, as `Ὑμῖν … τοῖς ἔθνεσιν` → *to you that are Gentiles* leaves it empty because `ὑμῖν` has written the *you*. So leave a displaced article `unrepresented` only where the ASV supplies it nothing else, which is the ordinary case and the one the examples above record.
amendments.why: Rule 20's flat *the article realizes nothing* is the sentence a verse pass reads first, and read alone it empties an article the ASV has plainly given a word. It did exactly that here: ROM.11.14 `μου τὴν σάρκα` → *them that are my flesh* was first returned with `τήν` `unrepresented` on rule 20 and had to be corrected to give the article the supplied antecedent pronoun *them*. Rules 89 and 92 already contain the correction — rule 89 says in terms that REV.19.5's article takes *ye* though `αὐτοῦ` occupies the possessive slot, because an address word is not a determiner a genitive pronoun can displace, and rule 92 assigns a separate antecedent pronoun to the article — but neither is where a reader deciding an article looks, and neither says what happens when the two configurations meet. The amendment scopes the emptying to the determiner slot, names the two supplied words that survive it with the rules that grant them, and adds the contrast case so the widening cannot be read as licensing an article a word some other token already spells: ROM.11.13 and 11.14 are the same recast construction one verse apart, and the article is empty in the first and aligned in the second precisely because `ὑμῖν` writes the antecedent in one and nothing writes it in the other. The genitive demonstrative is added to the displacer list on the same chapter's 11:30, and is only an instance of the principle the rule already states.

conventions: ROM.11 records no `added` unit. Every supplied English word in the chapter completes some source token's own English and is folded under rules 7 and 103: *of God* on χρηματισμός (11:4), *of them* on πρόσλημψις (11:15), *with them* on συγκοινωνός (11:17), *conceits* on ἑαυτοῖς (11:25), *time* on ποτε (11:30), *shown to* on ὑμετέρῳ (11:31), *again* on ἀνταποδοθήσεται (11:35). Where the fold repeats a pronoun the verse has already spent — *of them* at 11:15 against αὐτῶν at *casting away of them*, *with them* at 11:17 against αὐτοῖς at *among them* — rule 103's resumptive-pronoun contrast is what licenses it, and each unit's note names the `added` reading.

παραζηλόω is headed on *jealousy*, the resultative complement, at 11:11 and 11:14 alike; a head on *provoke* remains defensible and both notes say so. ἐλεάω is headed on *mercy* at 11:30, 11:31 and 11:32 on the same reasoning.

κατὰ φύσιν is one `aligned` unit wherever the ASV writes the single word *natural* (11:21, and 11:24's οἱ κατὰ φύσιν) and two units wherever it writes *by nature* (11:24's τῆς κατὰ φύσιν ἀγριελαίου). Rule 94's count of English words decides it, not the recurrence of the collocation; where the phrase is a verbless clause's predicate the supplied copula rides with it under rule 31.

report: Checked all 52 candidate groups. Every bucket carrying two treatments is licensed by a difference in the ASV's own wording, not by two analyses: κατὰ φύσιν as one word *natural* (11:21, 11:24 s020) against two words *by nature* (11:24 s006), decided by rule 94's count; ἐγκεντρίζω/ἐκκόπτω/ἐκκλάω with a bare preverb (11:19, 11:20, 11:22, 11:23), with a preverb particle *plus* a complete prepositional expression (11:17), and with a single prepositional expression that takes the whole particle (11:24 s004), which is rule 106's three arms; οὕτως with an answering καί (11:5, 11:31 → *even so* plus *also*) against οὕτως with none (11:26 → *so*), which is rule 100; and every article decided by whether a competing possessor or demonstrative stands (rules 20, 23, 38, 51, 60, 102). No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source licensing the difference, so patches is empty.

Read the dump end to end for the added/fold asymmetry the lemma table is blind to. ROM.11 contains no `added` unit at all: every supplied English word is folded onto a token whose English it completes — *of God* on χρηματισμός (11:4), *of them* on πρόσλημψις (11:15), *with them* on συγκοινωνός (11:17), *conceits* on ἑαυτοῖς (11:25), *time* on ποτε (11:30), *shown to* on ὑμετέρῳ (11:31), *again* on ἀνταποδοθήσεται (11:35). Two of these repeat a pronoun the verse has already spent (11:15, 11:17), and rule 103's resumptive-pronoun contrast is what licenses them; both notes name the `added` reading. The posture is uniform, so it is not a split, but it is recorded as a convention because it is exactly what a later reader cannot recover from the table.

Checked supplied copulas and subjects across the chapter's verbless clauses (11:6 twice, 11:11, 11:12, 11:15 twice, 11:16 twice, 11:27, 11:28 twice, 11:29, 11:33, 11:36 twice). Each is placed by what is left in its own clause to carry it and never off English word order: prepositional predicate to the preposition (11:6 ἐξ, 11:24 κατά, 11:36 εἰς), dative or predicate noun where no article stands to anchor it (11:6 χάριτι, 11:11 ἔθνεσιν, 11:36 αὐτῷ), predicate nominal or adjective where the subject is a noun (11:12, 11:15, 11:29, 11:33), predicate alone where no subject is expressed (11:28 twice), substantival demonstrative subject (11:27), and the subject noun where the apodosis is elliptical and borrows its predicate from the protasis (11:16 twice, rule 56). The article beside such a predicate keeps only its own determiner (11:11 τοῖς, rule 96). Consistent throughout.

Checked the rule 106 preverb decisions in eleven verbs. The accusative arm (11:7 *seeketh for*, 11:25 *ignorant of*, 11:32 *have mercy upon*) and the oblique arm (11:18 *over the branches* on the genitive's article, 11:22 *in his goodness* on the dative's article, 11:24 *into their own olive tree* on the dative noun) do not cross, and the particle rides inside the verb only where no expressed preposition or determiner-bearing article answers to it.

11:13 and 11:14 read the same recast construction consistently, and are the chapter's own evidence for the 11:14 correction: where the antecedent is an expressed ὑμῖν → *you*, the article gets nothing and the noun carries *that are* (11:13, rules 23, 92); where the ASV supplies the antecedent pronoun itself, the article takes *them* and the noun still keeps *that are … flesh* (11:14), the genitive μου keeping *my*. That combination is what the amendment below records.

BSB: 12 disagreements, none a genuine error, and no accepted edge was changed. Ten are documented convention differences — interrogative μή (rule 44, 11:1, 11:11), the nominalizing article of an articular infinitive (rule 61, 11:8 twice, 11:10), μέν (rule 70, 11:13), an article displaced by an expressed possessor (rules 20, 47, at 11:11 and 11:24), an article before a name or before determinerless *God* (rule 23, 11:29), and the duration idiom's article (rule 30, 11:36). The two prepositions are rule 36's own named exceptions: the four predicative εἰς of 11:9 are absorbed into the object complement the ASV writes bare (*a snare*, *a trap*, *a stumblingblock*, *a recompense*), and παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ at 11:27 is compressed into the possessive *my*, which the ASV's own gloss *the covenant from me* records.

One amendment, to rule 20; no new rule. Two head choices remain genuinely open and are named in their units rather than settled here: παραζηλόω on *jealousy* against *provoke* (11:11, 11:14), and the single *are* over three coordinate prepositional predicates placed on εἰς rather than ἐξ (11:36). διὰ παντός → *always* (11:10) is the one status call I weighed and left: *al-* could be read as answering to παντός, which would make it `aligned` under rule 39 as κατὰ φύσιν → *natural* is, but the compound has lexicalized to a temporal sense neither element spells, which is rule 81's test for keeping *therefore* and *hereafter* noncompositional.
